# Hindalco Industries Limited

<!-- Generated by `make client-docs`. Do not edit inside the markers. -->

Researched 2026-09-29 · status **partial** · Budget spent: search and document-fetch budget exhausted while trying to locate a working full FY2021-22 annual report PDF (two fetch attempts returned corrupted/incomplete files) and a project-wise CSR spend breakdown. FY2021-22 csr_year figures (prescribed_csr, spent_on_projects, admin_overheads, total_spent) were not found because the only accessible FY2021-22 statutory PDF omitted the CSR annexure table. Project/district-level csr_spend breakdown, a distinct stated_geography priority list, named grants, and PAN/CSR-1/Darpan identifiers were also not found in sources read.

Hindalco Industries Limited (CIN L27020MH1958PLC011238), the Aditya Birla Group's metals flagship, is confirmed as a distinct Section 135 CSR filer, recorded separately from any group-level 'Aditya Birla Group' entity, with parent_name noted as Aditya Birla Group. Statutory CSR annexure data was obtained for FY2023-24 (prescribed CSR ₹94.52 crore, total spent ₹47.86 crore, no impact assessment) and FY2022-23 (prescribed CSR ₹69.20 crore, obligation after set-off ₹45.14 crore, total spent ₹36.04 crore, no impact assessment) from the respective Integrated Annual Reports; FY2021-22 figures could not be retrieved because the only accessible PDF for that year omitted the CSR annexure and other candidate URLs failed to resolve. No project-level or state/district CSR spend breakdown was found in the text extracted; CSR is implemented via the Aditya Birla Centre for Community Initiatives and Rural Development (chaired by Rajashree Birla) and plant-adjacent entities such as Utkal Alumina Social Welfare Foundation, Kosala Livelihood and Social Foundation, and (in FY2021-22) Hindalco/Copper/Utkal Alumina Jan Seva Trusts — all logged as partners/implementing agencies, not merged with Hindalco. CSR footprint for FY2023-24 spans West Bengal, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana, Kerala and the UT of Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu, reaching a stated 622 villages, 17 urban slums and 1.3 million people. Four CSR themes (education, healthcare, sustainable livelihood, rural infrastructure/social development) and several office-bearer contacts (Rajashree Birla, Pragnya Ram, Satish Pai) were also recorded from Tier 1/2 sources with verbatim evidence and source URLs.

## What it set out to find

- legal name, CIN, domain identifiers
- csr_year data (section_135_applicable, average_net_profit, prescribed_csr, spent_on_projects, admin_overheads, total_spent, unspent_transferred, impact_assessment_done) for FY2023-24, FY2022-23, FY2021-22
- csr_spend by project/aggregate with sector, state, district, implementing agency, CSR-1
- footprint (plant-adjacent districts/states)
- stated priority geography, kept separate from footprint
- partners / implementing agencies (esp. Aditya Birla Centre for Community Initiatives and Rural Development and plant-level foundations)
- programs/themes
- metrics
- contacts
- documents
